description.value: The study compared brain activity during conditional and categorical syllogistic deductive reasoning, separately examining premise encoding and premise integration.

design.value: Event-related fMRI study using a within-participants comparison of conditional and syllogistic deductive problems and of encoding versus integration stages.

description.value: Twenty-six healthy subjects participated in the experiment. All were right-handed, had normal vision, with no neurological or psychiatric history.

consented_count.value: all participants gave written informed consent

task_description.value: Participants solved conditional and categorical syllogistic deductive problems involving two or three premises and four alternative conclusions, while fMRI activity was measured. Reasoning trials comprised encoding of premises and integration of premises to generate a conclusion; memory trials required literal recognition of a single premise.

instructions.value: Participants were asked to read each premise and whenever possible, to draw a new conclusion promptly and accurately; in memory trials, they were told to read and remember sentences carefully for fast recognition.

stimuli.value: Sentences described qualities of an unspecified “thing” using nonexistent two-syllabic Italian adjectives with plausible phonological structure; problems were conditional or quantified categorical syllogisms.

task_performance_measures.value: Average accuracy for conditional and main-set syllogistic problems
Reaction times on integrable and non-integrable sentences for both conditional and syllogistic problems

instrument.value: 3T Siemens Allegra head scanner (Siemens, Erlangen, Germany)

description.value: BOLD contrast was obtained using echo planar T2*-weighted imaging (EPI). Acquisition of 32 transverse slices provided coverage of the whole cerebral cortex. In-plane resolution was 3 mm × 3 mm; slice thickness and gap were 2.5 mm and 1.25 mm, respectively.

number_of_volumes.value: on average 1561 volumes for each subject, ranging from 1355 to 1748

description.value: The first four image volumes of each run were discarded. Images were realigned, slice-time corrected, normalized to MNI space using nonlinear warping in SPM2, and smoothed with an 8 mm FWHM Gaussian filter. Time series were high-pass filtered at 128 s and prewhitened using an autoregressive AR(1) model.

steps.value: discarded the first four image volumes of each run
nonlinear normalization to MNI space using SPM2
spatial smoothing with a Gaussian filter of 8 mm full-width at half maximum
prewhitening with an autoregressive AR(1) model

model_settings.value: The 18 event types were modeled as miniblocks with duration corresponding to the timing stimuli shown on screen. Stimulus functions were convolved with the standard SPM2 hemodynamic response function. Five additional factors modeled error trials separately from correct trials.

Participant contrast images underwent second-level ANOVAs for encoding and integration effects; linear compounds compared effects using between-subject variance. A random effects approach was used, with correction for nonsphericity.
PCA was run on average integration effects extracted from six regions of interest identified from the syllogistic integration activation map.

estimator.value: principal component analysis with varimax orthogonal rotation

description.value: Propositional reasoning problems using logical connectives, including conditional forms such as “if…then”.
Reasoning problems using quantified predicative statements such as “all X are Y” or “no X are Y”.
A premise was read with the explicit aim of using it for reasoning.
A sentence was read and remembered for literal recognition among four alternatives.
The second premise shared an adjectival term with the first premise, allowing generation of a deductive conclusion.
The second premise did not share an adjectival term with the first premise and could not be integrated with it.

interpretations.value: The network of areas active during integration of quantified sentences is not functionally homogeneous: at least two factors are needed to explain a substantial amount of the variance.
